annotations.text:
Wireframes for the kickoff doc, low fidelity on purpose — structure, flow and the rules that constrain them, not visual design.
Four pages: this map, then the owner editor, the admin console, and the tenant sites the renderer serves.
Red notes mark the decisions the doc says not to change without a very good reason.

Owner editor — phase 4, and the screen a customer actually lives in.
Category locks after first publish; template and palette stay switchable because a template may never invent a field.
Content is one generated form, so a new category costs zero frontend work. Publish is the paywall, not the front door.

Admin console — your console, not a customer's. TOTP mandatory, impersonation read-only and audited.
The registry screen (bottom right) is phase 2 and the load-bearing one: get it right and categories 5 through 45 are configuration.

Tenant sites — 90% of these visitors are on a mid-range Android, so these are the artboards that matter.
Showcase only: call, WhatsApp, directions, contact form, external link. No cart, ever.
RTL is the same template and the same JSON with dir flipped — built in from the first line of CSS, never retrofitted.
